title: Oncall telemetry‑guided triage and gradual failover safeguard
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce noisy pages and automate safe multi-region failover by combining telemetry-driven triage, proportional load-shedding policies, and an automated on-call runbook that can execute gradual failover safeguards. Deliverables: (1) scoring model for alert prioritization driven by tokenized telemetry and request context, (2) an orchestrated runbook execution path that gates aggressive failover behind progressive checks, (3) circuit-breaker/ shed thresholds that adapt to SLO drift and regional capacity signals.
rationale: Recent incidents showed excessive paging during transient regional overloads which caused operator fatigue and increased mean time to recovery. Blindly triggering failover caused cascading capacity constraints in secondary regions. We need a telemetry-aware decision path that (a) suppresses noisy low-impact signals, (b) elevates high-confidence SLO violations, and (c) executes gradual, reversible failover steps with automated safeguards.
scope: Implement alert scoring, integrate scoring into PagerDuty routing, create a runbook automation play that performs progressive failover and load-shedding, add dashboards and post-incident metrics to validate reduced noise and safer cutovers.
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of the entire alerting stack, replacement of third-party paging provider, major changes to customer-facing SLA language.
proposal_summary: Build a lightweight ML‑ish scoring engine (XGBoost/Logistic) using features: SLO deviation magnitude, error type (5xx vs 4xx), request origin region, request QPS volatility, cache miss spikes, KV cache eviction rate, circuit state, and historical alert noisiness. Use score buckets (Informational, Actionable, Escalate) to control routing. Tie the Escalate bucket to an automated canary-based failover playbook that runs staged actions (traffic fraction shift, instance scale, region read-only redirect) with automatic backout criteria based on real-time telemetry.
runbook_snippet: 1) Verify canary synthetic latency and error budget margin > 0. 2) If Escalate alerts >= 3 within 2m and canary failing, pause ingestion queue, enable proportional shed (5-30% by policy), notify oncall and kick off staged traffic shift (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 3m observation windows. 3) Abort and rollback if SLO recovery < threshold or error rate increases on target region.
acceptance_criteria: Score model reduces paging volume from metric-noise alerts by >= 40% in canary region
Automated staged failover can shift 10% -> 50% traffic in safe increments with automated rollback on negative signal
Oncall runbook completes without manual escalation in >= 2/3 simulated overload drills
New dashboards show SLO burn-rate, paging delta, and rollback frequency
milestones: Design review and scoring feature set - 2026-02-28
Implement runbook automation and circuit guard - 2026-03-12
risks_and_mitigations: False negative suppression could hide real incidents -> mitigation: escrow an 'urgent' override flag and run daily sampling of suppressed alerts for 24h
Automated failover could move failure to secondary region -> mitigation: traffic shift limited by capacity-aware caps and automatic rollback triggers based on SLO telemetry
Model drift over time -> mitigation: weekly retrain job and QA pipeline with historical incident labels
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring feature computation and PagerDuty routing mapping
Integration test against staging pager with synthetic noisy signals
Run three tabletop drills with oncall rotation and automated playbook enabled
Chaos test: induce KV cache eviction spike in staging and assert proportional shed and rollback behave as expected
rollout_plan: Feature flag scoring logic behind 'telemetry-triage' toggle
Ramp scoring in non-prod and small customer subset for 72h
Enable Escalate->Automatic Playbook in one low-risk region for a week
After validated metrics, promote to all regions and remove flag after 30 days
